headline.ci_method: Welch t interval over stores, promoted against control

gate.rule: Pass only if all three hold for the full difference-in-differences estimator (promoted item plus sibling, promotion plus post weeks, randomised control stores), fixed before results as the headline: (1) across 400 simulated campaigns its 95% interval covers the true incremental profit in at least 90% of them; (2) on the headline campaign its 95% interval excludes zero, so it makes a definite call; (3) that call has the same sign as the true incremental profit.

before_and_after_without_control.note: The promotion weeks fall on the seasonal peak, so a before-and-after view credits the season to the promotion.

manager_picked_stores.note: When the stores with the best trend get the promotion, their growth is credited to it.

caveats: Everything is simulated. Store sizes, the season, the lift, cannibalisation, pull-forward and the margins are chosen by the author, so the sizes of the results describe this setup, not any retailer.
One item, one sibling, one four-week promotion. No competing promotions, display or feature support, stock-outs, price ladders or halo on other categories.
Stores are independent. Real stores share distribution centres, media and shoppers, which can leak a promotion into control stores.
The promotion is randomised across stores in the headline campaign. The manager-picked variant shows what happens without that.
Margins and the discount are assumptions. Profit here ignores supplier funding, which often pays part of the discount.
Intervals assume stores are independent draws. They do not cover a mistaken choice of pre-period or post-period length.
